value.rationale: The central 2026 theorem reveals bounded averaging in genuinely nonlocally convex Lorentz sequence spaces, but does not determine when averaging is metrically contractive. Exact one-block contractivity versus two-block expansion identifies the minimal noncontractive block complexity, and the sharp binary two-block profile with exponentially small near-convex defect explains a mathematically natural singular geometry. This is not simply recomputing uniform boundedness, and does not claim an unrestricted sharp operator norm.
